name: Cash-Intensive Businesses
description: Use of businesses that naturally handle large cash volumes, such as restaurants, car washes, laundromats, vending, convenience stores and nail salons, to blend illicit cash with legitimate takings. Deposits are inflated to fit the business's apparent scale.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering Typologies: cash-intensive business guidance (general)
FinCEN, SAR Activity Review on cash-intensive businesses (general)
JMLSG Guidance Part II, sector guidance on cash-intensive customers (general)

indicators.name: Cash deposits exceed plausible business capacity
indicators.canon: Cash deposits exceed plausible business capacity
indicators.desc: Declared turnover or deposits are higher than the premises size, staffing, opening hours or stock purchases would support.
indicators.ctx: Declared turnover or deposits are higher than the premises size, staffing, opening hours or stock purchases would support.
indicators.fp: New or fast-growing businesses can legitimately outperform peers.

indicators.name: Deposits unsupported by supplier or cost-of-sales activity
indicators.canon: Deposits unsupported by supplier or cost-of-sales activity
indicators.desc: Cash takings are high but there are few payments to suppliers, rent, wages or tax authorities.
indicators.ctx: Cash takings are high but there are few payments to suppliers, rent, wages or tax authorities.
indicators.fp: Cash-paid suppliers or off-account costs may exist.

indicators.name: Sudden growth in cash volumes
indicators.desc: Step-change in deposit values or frequency without explanation such as new outlets or season.
indicators.ctx: Step-change in deposit values or frequency without explanation such as new outlets or season.
indicators.fp: Expansion, promotion or events can explain growth.

indicators.name: Business type inconsistent with location or customer base
indicators.canon: Business type inconsistent with location or customer base
indicators.desc: Cash business operating where demand appears limited, with few visible customers or irregular hours.
indicators.ctx: Cash business operating where demand appears limited, with few visible customers or irregular hours.
indicators.fp: Online-only operations or early-stage businesses may appear quiet.

indicators.name: Cash deposits mixed with unrelated third-party funds
indicators.canon: Payments from or to unrelated third parties
indicators.desc: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
indicators.ctx: Deposits include cheques, transfers or cash from persons unconnected to trading, or rotated across several business accounts.
indicators.fp: Owners may inject funds legitimately as capital.

indicators.name: Ownership or management opaque for cash business
indicators.canon: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified
indicators.desc: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.
indicators.ctx: Unclear beneficial owners, nominee directors or frequent ownership change in a cash business.
indicators.fp: Family businesses may have informal arrangements.

indicators.name: Large cash withdrawals paired with deposits of equivalent value
indicators.canon: Large cash withdrawals paired with deposits of equivalent value
indicators.desc: Cash is repeatedly withdrawn and redeposited, or round-tripped with associated accounts.
indicators.ctx: Cash is repeatedly withdrawn and redeposited, or round-tripped with associated accounts.
indicators.fp: Float management for tills may look similar.

indicators.name: Multiple cash businesses controlled by same people
indicators.desc: Several apparently separate businesses or sub-accounts share owners, signatories, addresses, devices or bank accounts.
indicators.ctx: Common owners or addresses across several cash businesses with cross-funding.
indicators.fp: Franchise or serial entrepreneurs are common.
